kinds.regulation: Read in the FIA 2026 Section C [Technical] PDF itself (Issue 19, in force at Silverstone). Article given; quote copied from the extracted PDF text. Every Issue 19 quote below was also found word for word in Issue 21 (2026-10-19) unless same_in_iss21 says otherwise.
kinds.official: Statement or document from the FIA, Formula 1, Red Bull, Ford or Red Bull Ford Powertrains (including a team spec sheet as reproduced by press).
kinds.reported: Reputable journalism (or Wikipedia). Not confirmed by the team or the FIA.
kinds.measured: Taken from public timing/telemetry already in this repo (concept/data/telemetry, OpenF1) or fetched from OpenF1 on the access date. One lap, about 3.7 Hz car_data, so treat as approximate.
kinds.derived: Arithmetic on regulation or measured numbers; method stated.
kinds.unknown: Not public. Value is null on purpose.

_meta.fetch_note: fetched=true: the page itself was opened on 2026-10-24 and the value read there. fetched=false: only a search-engine summary of the page was seen (page blocked or empty); treat as weaker.

regulation.value: 1600 cc (+0/-10 cc), 6 cylinders, 90 deg V, 4 valves/cyl, bore 80 mm
regulation.quote: Engine cubic capacity must be 1600cc (+0/−10cc). ... six cylinders arranged in a 90° “V” configuration ... The cylinder bore diameter must be 80mm (±0.1mm).
No cylinder ... may have a geometric compression ratio higher than 16.0 ... From 1 June 2026 to 31 December 2026: when the Engine is at ambient temperature as well as when the Engine is at 130degC.
regulation.note: The hot check from 1 June 2026 followed the early-season row over Mercedes and Red Bull Ford allegedly exceeding 16:1 when hot. Red Bull's Ben Hodgkinson called it noise; reports say RBPT later backed the clarification (planetf1_cr, search summary only).

regulation.article: C5.14 (and absence of any crank-speed cap in C5)
regulation.quote: Engine high rev limits may vary for differing conditions provided all are contained within a band of 750rpm.
regulation.note: Section C Issue 19 has no maximum crankshaft speed. C5.14 only requires all high rev limits to sit within a 750 rpm band. The only '15 000rpm' in the text is C9.8.2, a launch-gear test speed, not a limit. In effect the cap is fuel: C5.2.4 lets fuel energy flow rise with rpm only up to 10,500 rpm (0.27*10500+165 = 3000 MJ/h), so extra revs bring no extra fuel energy. Motor Sport Magazine (mmag_engines) and the Wikipedia RB22 infobox (wiki_rb22) print '15,000 rpm'; that wording was not found in Issue 19 or 21 and is probably carried over from the 2014-2025 rules.

regulation.quote: Fuel energy flow must not exceed 3000MJ/h, with a maximum energy flow per cylinder never exceeding 550MJ/h under normal operating conditions.
Below 10500rpm the fuel energy flow must not exceed EF(MJ/h)=0.27*N(rpm)+ 165
Engine intake air pressure must be less than 4.8 barA at all times.

regulation.value: single-stage single turbo, max 150,000 rpm, no energy taken off the turbo shaft
regulation.quote: The energy of the rotating parts of the Turbo Charger may not be transferrable to any other component. ... The rotational speed of the Turbo Charger may not exceed 150,000rpm.
The use of any device, other than the engine described in C5.1 above, and the ERS-K, to propel the car and/or Recharge energy, is not permitted.
regulation.note: The term MGU-H does not appear in Issue 19 or Issue 21. formula1.com: the new unit 'deletes the MGU-H' (f1_pu_explainer).

regulation.quote: The absolute electrical DC power of the ERS-K may not exceed 350kW.
regulation.derived: C5.2.21 applies a fixed 0.97 electrical-to-mechanical efficiency in the Standard ECU, so 350 kW DC is treated as about 339.5 kW mechanical.

regulation.quote: P(kW) = 1800 – 5 * car speed (kph) when the car speed is below 340kph
regulation.derived: Full 350 kW up to 290 km/h; 300 kW at 300 km/h; 250 kW at 310 km/h; 100 kW at 340 km/h.

regulation.quote: P(kW) = 7100 – 20 * car speed (kph) when the car speed is below 355kph

regulation.value: P = 250 kW below 310 km/h, then base taper
regulation.note: Race/Sprint only, FIA-named sectors. Silverstone: T1-T4 (350-1000 m) and T15-T16 (4950-5450 m) per fia_gbr_pu_info. Issue 21 adds 'during any power limited period'.

regulation.quote: The MGU-K mechanical torque magnitude may not exceed 500Nm.
The difference between the maximum and the minimum state of charge of the ES may not exceed 4MJ at any time the car is on the track.

regulation.note: Silverstone 2026 (fia_gbr_pu_info): 6.5 MJ in SQ/Q, 8.0 MJ race/sprint, 8.5 MJ with Overtake, 8.5 MJ in FP.
There is no ICE power cap; ICE output is bounded only through fuel energy flow. An Italian site describing '400 kW' as a regulatory limit is wrong on this point.

official_statements.value: Ford provides expertise 'including battery cell and electric motor technology as well as power unit control software and analytics'

Ford contributes 12 components across several PU systems (MGU-K parts, turbo hardware, 3D-printed water pipes and exhaust parts), load simulation, energy-split simulation software, and battery charge-cycle software; Ford staff attend battery tests
official_statements.note: Quotes Ford chief engineer Christian Hertrich: 'Insgesamt steuern wir 12 Komponenten in verschiedenen Systemen zur Power Unit bei.' More than 600 people at Milton Keynes.

official_statements.value: A sixth-generation DM01 was on the dyno running Barcelona race simulations on launch night (15 Jan 2026); aim for the first test was 'trouble-free'
official_statements.note: Ben Hodgkinson (RBPT technical director). No dated first-fire-up milestone was found in an official release.

redbull.com table row for the RB22 prints '10000+hp/745kW' (the hp figure is evidently a typo for about 1000 hp). Not stated as a measured DM01 figure; says only that the hybrid unit produces about 50% of the power.

official_statements.value: Best-performing ICE of 2026 (period 1, to Canada): Mercedes 2-4% below it; Audi, Ferrari and Honda more than 4% below it. Period 2 (to Hungary): no new homologations granted.
official_statements.note: The FIA text does not name the benchmark; Sky Sports (sky_aduo, 7 Jun 2026) and Auto Action (autoaction_aduo) report it is Red Bull Ford, which received no ADUO upgrades. The index is ICE-only (engine speed, input shaft torque, MGU-K power, lap-time power sensitivity; f1_aduo_explainer) and formula1.com says it is 'not representative of full power unit performance'. Period 3 (Netherlands to Mexico City) not yet published.
Not named by Red Bull, Ford or press in anything found. Ford's stated role covers cell technology expertise and charge-cycle software, not cell manufacture.

reported_performance.note: Generic 2026 ICE figure in a regulation explainer, not a DM01 measurement. No outlet found publishes a DM01-specific ICE kW figure.

reported_performance.value: benchmark ICE; Mercedes 2-4% lower; Ferrari/Honda/Audi >4% lower (first half of 2026)
reported_performance.note: From the FIA ADUO index (fia_aduo) plus press identification of the benchmark. Mekies still says Mercedes has 'the most powerful power unit' overall (autoaction_aduo), i.e. ICE plus ERS use.
Not a sourced estimate. Envelope = 833 kW fuel power (C5.2.3) x assumed brake efficiency 0.45-0.50; the 400 kW press figure sits inside it (48%). Use as a sensitivity range, not as data.

HAD, 5th gear. Other teams on the same session: ANT 12172, LEC 12080, NOR 12579, LAW (same PU) 12194. Full-throttle rpm in 6th-8th spans about 9,000-12,200.

aero_concept.value: Low-drag concept; strong in low-speed corners and traction, less clear in medium/high-speed corners; aero degradation flagged by Verstappen at Monza

Small sidepods ('certainly smaller than most, but zero? Not really'), heavily slotted bargeboards pulling flow from under the front floor, small floor louvres ahead of the rear tyre, cut-out in the diffuser side
Pushrod front, pushrod rear (Gary Anderson, after the Barcelona test; GPFans/AutoRacer also report double pushrod)
aero_concept.note: Conflict: Wikipedia infobox lists pull-rod front / push-rod rear (wiki_rb22). The photo-based Anderson reading is preferred; no team statement found.

aero_concept.value: From Miami: rotating upper flap that turns 'up and over from the rear', centre-mounted actuator on the mainplane; reported rotation about 160-180 deg
aero_concept.note: Angle figures come from search summaries and disagree (160 vs 180 deg). Regulation: two fixed positions, <=400 ms transition, fails to Corner Mode (C3.11.6).

aero_concept.value: Rear wing did not return to Corner Mode: VER qualifying crash in Austria (R8) and VER race crash at Stowe, Silverstone (R9). Mekies: Silverstone was 'a different type of failure'. Both drivers reverted to an older wing spec for Spa.

value: R4 Miami: rotating rear wing, revised sidepods, front wing and corner inlets, floor, engine cover; big mass reduction (gpblog_miami, therace_overweight)
R8 Austria: new sidepod inlet with revised floor and rear suspension fairings (f1technical_austria, search summary)
R9 Silverstone: rear wheel bodywork winglets, number of cascade elements changed (fia_car_pres)
R15 Baku: package Mekies called part of steady development, closing most of the early ~1 s gap (therace_surge)

aero_concept.note: No drag or downforce coefficients, aero balance or Straight Mode drag delta are public for any 2026 car.
